s04 — does disabling soft-clipping change SNP recovery? (chr19)

library(ggplot2); library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(readr); library(knitr)
source("analyses/lib/design.r")   # bartheme(), corecol(); knit from the project root

Provenance

  • Rendered from commit 761a36dcb53d (branch mason2-sims) on 2026-10-26 13:03

1 Question & design

Does gatk’s high-divergence SNP loss come from soft-clipped bases being ignored? A read that carries divergent bases toward its end is often soft-clipped there by the aligner; those bases stay in the BAM but a caller may or may not use them. One hypothesis for why gatk (HaplotypeCaller) recovers fewer divergent SNPs than bcftools/freebayes is that soft-clipping starves it of the alt allele. This section tests that hypothesis directly, and in isolation.

The test is paired on a single BAM. For each divergence we take the existing s01 iter-1 gatk BAM (SNP-only data, seed 42, 30×) and run HaplotypeCaller on it twice:

  • gatk_default — HaplotypeCaller’s default, which uses soft-clipped bases.
  • gatk_nosoftclip — the same command plus --dont-use-soft-clipped-bases, which ignores them.

Because both calls see the identical alignment (same reads, same clips, same mapping), any difference in recovery is attributable to the flag alone — nothing else changes. We score each call against the controlled truth with analyses/lib/compare_vcfs.py (match on POS/REF/ALT after bcftools norm), and read out SNP-divergence recall (div_tp / n_truth_div) and het recall (het_tp / n_truth_het). Driver: analyses/s04-softclip/run_softclip_toggle.sh <DIV>.

Scope & assumptions.

  • Two divergences, D ∈ {0.06, 0.10} — the regime where gatk’s deficit is largest and where a clipping effect, if any, should be most visible. H = 0.005, 30×, iteration 1 only (single-shot; this is a caller-flag test, not an iteration test).
  • Only gatk is toggled — it is the caller with the deficit; the flag is a HaplotypeCaller option.
  • Prediction from the assembler-not-clipping account (see the s01/s02 read-fate sections: the SNPs gatk misses mostly have the base present at their position — they are assembler-limited, not alignment/clipping-limited): recall should barely move.
res <- "analyses/s04-softclip/results/"
sc <- bind_rows(lapply(c("0.06", "0.10"), function(d)
        read_csv(paste0(res, "softclip-toggle-", d, ".csv"), col_types = cols()))) %>%
  mutate(mode = sub("gatk_", "", caller),                       # default | nosoftclip
         mode = factor(mode, levels = c("default", "nosoftclip")),
         div_recall = div_tp / n_truth_div,                     # SNP divergence recall
         het_recall = het_tp / n_truth_het)                     # SNP het recall

2 Result: disabling soft-clipping does not recover the missed SNPs

sc %>%
  select(divergence, mode, `SNP divergence` = div_recall, `SNP het` = het_recall) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(`SNP divergence`, `SNP het`), names_to = "site", values_to = "recall") %>%
  ggplot(aes(factor(divergence), recall, fill = mode)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), width = 0.62, color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.15) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * recall)),
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), vjust = -0.4, size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~ site) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = corecol(pal = "wilke", numcol = 2),
                    labels = c("default (uses clipped bases)", "--dont-use-soft-clipped-bases"),
                    name = "HaplotypeCaller") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "divergence (D)", y = "recall (of true sites)",
       title = "Soft-clip toggle on the SAME BAM: recall is essentially unchanged") +
  bartheme()

The bars are visually indistinguishable. The change from disabling soft-clipped bases, in the paired counts, is:

sc %>%
  group_by(divergence) %>%
  summarize(
    `div recall default`    = sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * div_recall[mode == "default"]),
    `div recall nosoftclip` = sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * div_recall[mode == "nosoftclip"]),
    `Δ div_tp (sites)`      = div_tp[mode == "nosoftclip"] - div_tp[mode == "default"],
    `het recall default`    = sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * het_recall[mode == "default"]),
    `Δ het_tp (sites)`      = het_tp[mode == "nosoftclip"] - het_tp[mode == "default"],
    `Δ false positives`     = fp[mode == "nosoftclip"] - fp[mode == "default"],
    .groups = "drop") %>%
  kable(caption = "Effect of --dont-use-soft-clipped-bases (nosoftclip − default). Negative Δ = disabling clipped bases HURTS.",
        table.attr = 'class="center"', format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
Effect of –dont-use-soft-clipped-bases (nosoftclip − default). Negative Δ = disabling clipped bases HURTS.
divergence div recall default div recall nosoftclip Δ div_tp (sites) het recall default Δ het_tp (sites) Δ false positives
0.06 90.04% 90.04% 107 89.56% -64 26
0.10 70.34% 69.96% -23,464 68.88% -3,236 -2,846

Interpretation. Ignoring soft-clipped bases does not rescue the SNPs gatk misses — it moves recall by a fraction of a percent, and in the wrong direction:

  • D = 0.06: div recall 90.04% → 90.04% (Δ = +107 sites, +0.003%). No effect.
  • D = 0.10: div recall 70.34% → 69.96% (Δ = −23,464 sites, −0.5% relative). Disabling clipped bases slightly lowers recall, and het recall likewise (68.9% → 67.8%). The one thing that improves is false positives (fewer, because fewer bases means fewer calls).

If soft-clipping were starving the caller of the alt allele, removing the (already-used) clipped bases could only make things worse, and using them should be what helps — which is exactly the sign we see, but the magnitude is tiny. The decisive point is the null: the ~30% of divergent SNPs gatk fails to recover at D = 0.10 are not hiding in soft-clipped bases. Toggling how the caller treats those bases recovers essentially none of them. This is a fourth independent line — alongside the caller-swap (bcftools/freebayes recover gatk’s misses from the same BAMs), the caller-independent read classification, and the per-variant read-fate result (gatk’s not-called SNPs mostly have the base already aligned at their position) — that gatk’s high-divergence deficit is its reference-anchored local reassembler failing on divergent sequence, not soft-clipping upstream.

3 Does it hold across iterations?

The test above is iteration 1 — deliberately, because that is where soft-clipping is maximal: the reads are mapped against the raw reference at full divergence. As iteration proceeds the consensus converges toward the sample, the effective divergence to the mapping target drops, and soft-clipping falls with it (the read-fate sections show gatk’s called-SNP clipping collapsing across iterations). So iter 1 is the strongest possible test — but we confirm the toggle stays inert once clipping has mostly disappeared.

How iter ≥ 2 is scored. At iteration k the gatk BAM is mapped to consensus_{k-1}, so we call HaplotypeCaller against that consensus (default vs --dont-use-soft-clipped-bases) and score the cumulative recovered set the way the s01 pipeline defines it: recovered_k = the set already baked into consensus_{k-1} (identical for both arms) ∪ the new hom-alt SNP calls. Only iter-k calling is toggled, so any difference is the flag alone. (s01 is SNP-only, so the consensus keeps reference coordinates — no liftover. Driver: run_softclip_toggle_iter.sh <DIV> <ITER>.)

iters <- c(1, 2, 3)
sweep <- bind_rows(lapply(c("0.06", "0.10"), function(d)
  bind_rows(lapply(iters, function(k) {
    f <- if (k == 1) paste0(res, "softclip-toggle-", d, ".csv")
         else        paste0(res, "softclip-toggle-", d, "-iter", k, ".csv")
    read_csv(f, col_types = cols())                       # fails loudly if a run is missing
  })))) %>%
  mutate(mode = factor(sub("gatk_", "", caller), levels = c("default", "nosoftclip")),
         div_recall = div_tp / n_truth_div)
ggplot(sweep, aes(iteration, div_recall, color = mode, group = mode)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) + geom_point(size = 2.6) +
  facet_wrap(~ divergence, labeller = label_both) +
  scale_color_manual(values = corecol(pal = "wilke", numcol = 2),
                     labels = c("default", "--dont-use-soft-clipped-bases"), name = "HaplotypeCaller") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = iters) + scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = "mapping iteration", y = "cumulative SNP divergence recall",
       title = "Soft-clip toggle stays inert as iteration converges the consensus") +
  bartheme()

sweep %>% group_by(divergence, iteration) %>%
  summarize(`div recall default`    = sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * div_recall[mode == "default"]),
            `div recall nosoftclip` = sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * div_recall[mode == "nosoftclip"]),
            `Δ div_tp (sites)`      = div_tp[mode == "nosoftclip"] - div_tp[mode == "default"],
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  kable(caption = "Soft-clip toggle effect on cumulative div recall, by iteration (nosoftclip − default).",
        table.attr = 'class="center"', format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
Soft-clip toggle effect on cumulative div recall, by iteration (nosoftclip − default).
divergence iteration div recall default div recall nosoftclip Δ div_tp (sites)
0.06 1 90.04% 90.04% 107
0.06 2 93.24% 93.24% 131
0.06 3 93.77% 93.77% 188
0.10 1 70.34% 69.96% -23,464
0.10 2 79.45% 79.49% 2,838
0.10 3 80.97% 81.09% 7,232

Interpretation. Iteration lifts recall enormously (D=0.10: 70% → 81% — the point of the whole project), while the soft-clip toggle stays within ±0.5% at every iteration. Its effect is not just small but inconsistent in sign: at D=0.10 disabling clipped bases costs 23k sites single-shot (−0.38% of truth), then flips to a negligible +2.8k / +7.2k (+0.05% / +0.12%) at iterations 2–3, and at D=0.06 it is a trivial positive throughout. That is the opposite of what a real clipping limitation would look like — a consistent, sizable gain from using the clipped bases. A sign-flipping, noise-level wobble is what you see when the flag simply doesn’t matter. The conclusion is iteration-independent: soft-clipping is not what limits gatk’s divergent-SNP recovery, single-shot or iterated; iteration, not the caller’s clip policy, is the lever that moves recall.

4 The toggle is gatk-specific: bcftools and freebayes

--dont-use-soft-clipped-bases is a HaplotypeCaller option, and there is no equivalent to run for the other two callers — not by omission, but by construction:

  • bcftools mpileup builds its pileup from the aligned portion of each read; soft-clipped bases (CIGAR S) are simply not in the pileup. bcftools is therefore already in the “don’t use soft-clipped bases” regime, always.
  • freebayes assembles haplotypes from the aligned reads and likewise does not use soft-clipped sequence; it exposes no soft-clip toggle.

So there is nothing to toggle — and the existing evidence already settles the question for them. In the caller-swap result, bcftools and freebayes (which never use soft-clipped bases) recover ~99 % of the divergent SNPs gatk misses from the same BAMs. If ignoring soft-clipped bases were a recovery handicap, the callers that always ignore them could not be the ones that recover more. Where bcftools/freebayes do miss SNPs, the per-variant read-fate analysis shows the cause is alignment: the read is clipped off the site or mapped elsewhere, so the alt base isn’t present at the position at all. That is an upstream mapping loss — the divergent bases were clipped away during alignment and aren’t reliably placed at the site — not a caller policy of ignoring bases that are present. No soft-clip flag, on any caller, recovers a base that alignment removed. This is why iteration (which re-anchors those reads) is the lever that helps the pileup/haplotype callers, exactly as the read-fate sections show.

5 Summary

  • Re-calling the same iter-1 BAM with vs without --dont-use-soft-clipped-bases changes SNP divergence recall by +0.003% (D=0.06) and −0.5% (D=0.10) — i.e. not at all, or slightly worse.
  • The same holds at iterations 2 and 3: the toggle’s effect stays a fraction of a percent as the consensus converges and clipping falls, so the conclusion is iteration-independent.
  • The flag is gatk-specific; bcftools and freebayes never use soft-clipped bases yet recover most of what gatk misses, so “not using clipped bases” is not a recovery handicap. Their residual misses are alignment-limited (base clipped-off / mismapped), upstream of any caller flag.
  • Soft-clipping is therefore not the mechanism behind gatk’s high-divergence SNP loss; the deficit is caller-side (assembler), consistent with the s01/s02 read-fate analyses.
  • Practical takeaway: --dont-use-soft-clipped-bases is not a useful lever for recovering divergent SNPs here (it trades a sliver of recall for slightly fewer false positives).

5.1 Data dictionary

analyses/s04-softclip/results/softclip-toggle-<D>.csv — two rows per file (gatk_default, gatk_nosoftclip), one compare_vcfs.py summary each, scored on the same BAM. Columns (SNP subset used here; indel columns are all zero because this is SNP-only s01 data):

column meaning
region, coverage, divergence, heterozygosity, seed simulation condition (chr19, 30×, D, H=0.005, seed 42)
caller gatk_default or gatk_nosoftclip (the toggle)
iteration mapping iteration (1 = single-shot)
n_truth_div number of true SNP divergence (1|1) sites
div_tp divergence sites called hom-alt with matching allele (recovered)
div_het divergence sites called heterozygous
div_ref_or_absent divergence sites called hom-ref or not called — reference bias / loss
div_other divergence hom-alt wrong allele / edge case
n_truth_het number of true SNP het (0|1) sites
het_tp het sites called heterozygous (recovered)
het_hom_alt / het_ref_or_absent / het_other het site miscall outcomes
fp called SNP variants matching no truth site (false positives)
n_called_snp total confident SNP calls
n_truth_indel_*, indel_*, fp_indel, n_called_indel indel counterparts (all 0 here)

Derived in this notebook: div_recall = div_tp / n_truth_div, het_recall = het_tp / n_truth_het, mode = the toggle parsed from caller.
